item.title: eMudhra to exit global SSL/TLS certificate business
item.description:
📝 Will Sharpen Focus on Core Enterprise Solutions and trust services other than SSL/TLS BENGALURU, INDIA, October 22, 2026 - eMudhra Limited (BSE: 543533 | NSE: EMUDHRA), a global digital trust company, today announced that its Board has decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. He added that global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1% of the global revenue. Core businesses unaffected eMudhra’s global SSL/TLS infrastructure runs separately from its other operations.
🔗 Read more: https://emudhra.com/en/press-release/emudhra-to-exit-global-ssl-tls-certificate-business

item.title: Jailbreaking the Switch 2
item.description:
📝 To my knowledge, it’s the first such exploit for the Switch 2. This was a Switch 1 game, so the SmileBASIC agent could work on the exploit on my Switch 1, while the WebKit agent worked on the Switch 2. We don’t have their code, so it’s unclear which sysmodules have which privileges.
🔗 Read more: https://pepsipu.com/blog/2026-10-switch2-jailbreak-ns2jb/

item.title: Several Linux kernel vulnerabilities accidentally posted to public mailing list
item.description:
📝 Several Linux Kernel Vulnerabilities Accidentally Posted To Public Kernel Mailing List Written by Michael Larabel in Linux Security on 22 October 2026 at 06:05 AM EDT. 12 Comments Seemingly as an accident, overnight several new Linux kernel vulnerability reports were posted to the public Linux kernel mailing list rather than the private security mailing list. Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative sent out a number of vulnerability reports to the public Linux kernel mailing list (LKML) rather than the typical private security mailing list.
🔗 Read more: https://www.phoronix.com/news/LKML-New-Trend-Vulnerabilities

item.title: SBD: We Have a Filesystem at Home
item.description:
📝 JuiceFS just held the image. So a Sprite’s disk was chunks, plus a metadata database saying which chunks made up each image, plus a checkpoint database saying which image was which. Just a disk Enter: the Sprites Block Device (SBD).
🔗 Read more: https://fly.io/blog/sprites-block-device/
